# Pinned to non-heir-backoff=1.5 (the v1 default): this file tests v1's
# "non-heirs back off so the heir fires first" ordering. Since
# DESIGN_UPDATE.md D3 the default is 1.0 (stock timers), which only keeps
# the heir first once D1's short heir timeout lands.

# T6.2 (TASKS.md) -- DESIGN.md §3 degenerate-case table, row "Heir
# partitioned with old leader's minority": the heir can't win a majority
# from inside the minority side; the majority side, once its (backed-off,
# heir-biased) timeout expires, elects independently via a vanilla-style
# single-candidate campaign. Both halves are exercised in one file so the
# "can't win" and "does win" outcomes are directly comparable.
#
# 5 voters so a genuine minority (2) vs majority (3) split exists: {1,2}
# (old leader + heir) vs {3,4,5}. From the point the partition is imposed,
# every `stabilize` call below is scoped to one side of the split only --
# `Stabilize` (rafttest/interaction_env_handler_stabilize.go) delivers and
# processes traffic only for the node IDs passed to it, so a message
# addressed across the boundary is simply left sitting undelivered in the
# queue -- but only until some *later* stabilize call happens to include
# that recipient too, at which point it would be delivered after all
# (Stabilize doesn't care when a message was queued, only who it's
# addressed to). Since both sides get their own stabilize call later in
# this file, any cross-partition message must be explicitly dropped via
# deliver-msgs the moment it's generated, not just left unscoped -- an
# earlier draft of this file skipped that and produced a false result
# (the majority side silently granting a vote to the unreachable minority
# candidate, from a stale queued message, before the majority's own
# candidate ever got a chance).

log-level error
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3,4,5) index=2 heir-election=true stability-score=50 non-heir-backoff=1.5
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3,4,5) index=2 heir-election=true stability-score=255 non-heir-backoff=1.5
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3,4,5) index=2 heir-election=true stability-score=100 non-heir-backoff=1.5
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3,4,5) index=2 heir-election=true stability-score=90 non-heir-backoff=1.5
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3,4,5) index=2 heir-election=true stability-score=80 non-heir-backoff=1.5
----
ok

heir=2 churn=0

# Partition begins here: {1,2} (old leader + heir) vs {3,4,5} (majority).
# Node 1 keeps believing it's leader and keeps ticking/heartbeating -- it's
# alive, just cut off -- but from here on no `stabilize` call ever spans
# both sides again.

# The heir's own biased timeout (electionTimeout + tiny jitter) fires within
# one round, so it campaigns first, same as the happy-path crash case.
tick-election 2
----
ok

# Only the minority side is stabilized: 2's MsgVote reaches 1 (grants --
# same log, hasn't voted this term).
stabilize 1 2
----
> 2 handling Ready

  HardState Term:2 Vote:2 Commit:3
  Messages:
  1->2 MsgVoteResp Term:2 Log:0/0
> 2 receiving messages
  1->2 MsgVoteResp Term:2 Log:0/0

# 2's MsgVote copies addressed to 3/4/5 are still queued from the round
# above -- drop them outright (genuinely lost in transit, not merely
# delayed) so the majority's own stabilize call below can't accidentally
# deliver a stale minority candidacy to the majority side (an earlier
# draft of this file skipped this and produced a false result: 4 and 5
# silently granting a vote to the unreachable minority candidate from this
# leftover message, before the majority's own candidate ever got a
# chance).
deliver-msgs drop=(3,4,5)
----
dropped: 2->3 MsgVote Term:2 Log:1/3
dropped: 2->4 MsgVote Term:2 Log:1/3
dropped: 2->5 MsgVote Term:2 Log:1/3

# 2 has only 2 of 5 votes (itself + 1) -- short of the 3-vote majority.
# The heir cannot win from inside the minority.
raft-state
----
1: StateFollower (Voter) Term:2 Lead:0
2: StateCandidate (Voter) Term:2 Lead:0
3: StateFollower (Voter) Term:1 Lead:1
4: StateFollower (Voter) Term:1 Lead:1
5: StateFollower (Voter) Term:1 Lead:1

# Majority side: 3, 4 and 5 last heard from the leader before the
# partition, when heir 2 was believed live, so their frozen
# randomizedElectionTimeout is the backed-off (non-heir) value, not vanilla
# -- ticking one round (3 ticks) must not be enough on its own. Only 3 is
# advanced, matching the determinism trick used in heir_dead_fallback.txt
# (2 rounds guarantees crossing the backoff range regardless of the random
# draw, while never accumulating enough ticks toward a second, spurious
# campaign).
tick-election 3
----
ok
